title: Active Factors of Psychotherapy - Interpersonal Skills in psychotherapy with children and adolescents
summary: The focus on Interpersonal Skills of psychotherapists is one approach to improve the effectiveness of therapies. These Interpersonal Skills are usually often collected through self-report or standardized tasks. There are differing results to conceptual theories behind these Interpersonal Skills in the existing scientific literature and it is not thoroughly clear how much their usage differs between different patients of the same therapist. In step one we want to test if Interpersonal Skills should be seen as unified construct or in variying facets and to analyze and compare the influence of therapists and patients; in step two we want to put these into a context of other psychotherapy process variables like therapeutic relationship & clinical improvement and symptomatology.
conditions: All patients have a mental health disorder (at least one F-diagnosis accordng to ICD-10) and an indication for outpatient psychotherapy.

interventions.name: All patients received psychotherapy in the outpatient unit for children and adolescents of Trier University

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
-Patients needed to receive treatment at the outpatient unit for child and adolescent psychotherapy at Trier University, Germany at one time-point.
-There need to be at least three usable videos of therapy sessions.
-Patients under 15 years: active consent of the custodians to the recording and scientific processing of videos
-Patients at least 15 years: active consent of patients to the recording and scientific processing of videos
Exclusion criteria:
Unclear consent or objection to recording and scientific processing of videos.
